method.headerName: Name declared by the telescope in the file

plateSolve.title: Position in the sky
plateSolve.descriptionLocal: The file does not say precisely which part of the sky it shows, so objects cannot be marked on the image. StarLight can work it out by comparing the stars in the photo with those in a catalog. The Plate solve button first uses the installed local stars, without the internet. If they are not enough, as often happens with narrow fields, it switches to the online Gaia catalog, provided internet access is allowed.
plateSolve.descriptionOnline: The file does not say precisely which part of the sky it shows, so objects cannot be marked on the image. StarLight can work it out by comparing the stars in the photo with those in a catalog. The button uses the online Gaia catalog, which requires an internet connection; the request can take up to a minute. To do it without the internet, install or re-enable the “Stars for plate solving” package in the Deep-sky catalogs tab of the plugin gallery.

empty.title: No object recognized
empty.noFrame: Open a frame to find out which celestial object it contains.
empty.notRecognized: The file declares neither a known object nor coordinates that can be matched against the catalog of {count} available objects.

main.title: Main object
main.magnitudeHint: Apparent brightness of the object. The lower the number, the brighter the object
main.sizeHint: Measured in arcminutes, that is sixtieths of a degree. The full Moon is about thirty across

field.title: Field of view
field.sizeHint: Portion of sky captured, in arcminutes

others.title: Other objects in the field
others.description: Catalog objects whose coordinates fall within the framing.

overlay.title: Overlay
overlay.description: In fields crowded with objects, StarLight labels only the most important ones, groups nearby ones and limits the unnamed circles. The density and types chosen here also apply to the image exported with markers.

coordinates.title: Coordinates on the image
coordinates.description: Computed from the astrometric solution, like the markers. The grid shows the lines of right ascension and declination with their values at the edges; the orientation shows north and east; the scale bar shows an angular measure. In the Export step you can include them in PNG, JPEG and WebP files.
coordinates.gridHint: Lines of right ascension and declination, with values along the edges
coordinates.orientationHint: Two arrows showing north (N) and east (E) in the captured sky
coordinates.scaleBarHint: A line with its angular measure, in arcseconds, arcminutes or degrees

density.essentialHint: Only the main objects, with half the names and circles
density.normalHint: About ten names over a full field, plus a few circles
density.richHint: Twice the names and circles, for fields worth exploring

markerTypes.label: Object types shown
markerTypes.hide: Hides markers of this type (the capture target stays)
